def thanos_sort_max_length(n, arr):
    # Initialize a DP table where dp[mask] represents the maximum length of a sorted subarray
    # that can be obtained using the elements represented by the bitmask 'mask'.
    dp = [0] * (1 << n)
    
    # Iterate over all possible subsets of the array
    for mask in range(1 << n):
        # Check if the current subset is sorted
        subset = [arr[i] for i in range(n) if mask & (1 << i)]
        if subset == sorted(subset):
            dp[mask] = len(subset)
    
    # Iterate over all possible subsets to find the maximum length of a sorted subarray
    # that can be obtained by removing either the first or the second half of the array
    for mask in range(1 << n):
        half_size = n // 2
        # Try removing the first half
        first_half_mask = mask & ((1 << half_size) - 1)
        # Try removing the second half
        second_half_mask = mask & ~((1 << half_size) - 1)
        
        # Update the DP table considering the removal of either half
        dp[mask] = max(dp[mask], dp[first_half_mask], dp[second_half_mask])
    
    # The answer is the maximum value in the DP table
    return max(dp)
